This coherence is pair-specific and goes beyond the shared Grade/Term/Skill Area hierarchy, the zero-gap rank co-location, the shared page-120/table-row source proximity, and the weak trigram overlap that nominated the pair. buildsTowards is not taken: nothing in either statement, their Learning Components, or their source refs evidences that proficiency in tool management (pencil, eraser, ruler) extends into, or is developmentally required for, composing a ten-sentence creative text; they are concurrently taught parallel Term 2 requirements rather than an earlier capability substantively deepened into a later one, and the reverse direction is likewise unsupported. relatesTo is symmetric and retains the canonical endpoint order. These limit certainty but do not contradict the Grade 3 / Term 2 / Writing placement relied on here.

judgment.rationale: First SFI: Grade 1 / Term 4 / Reading and Phonics / Daily Phonic Activities (Phonics) — 'Revises common consonant digraphs (sh, ch and th) at the beginning of a word. For example, sh-ip, ch-ip, th-in' (LC tags: digraphs, initial sounds, phonics, revision). Second SFI: Grade 1 / Term 3 / same Skill Area and Phonics sub-strand — 'Uses consonant blends to build up and break down words (e.g. r and l blends- bl-ack, fl-op, sl-ip etc.)' (LCs: building words; breaking down words; tags consonant blends, building words, segmenting, phonics). Both are resolved Grade 1 (rank 1), so direction would be constrained to Term 3 -> Term 4, but the evidence does not show substantive extension of one capability by the other: blends and digraphs are distinct grapheme-phoneme categories, and the Term 4 statement revises digraphs that the Term 3 table-row context records as introduced in Term 3 by a separate printed item, not by this blends statement. The dependency claim would therefore rest on sibling/row content rather than the second endpoint itself. What the evidence does support is genuine pair-specific coherence: adjacent terms of the same grade, same Skill Area and Daily Phonic Activities sub-strand, both working with multi-letter consonant onsets in word building and breaking (sl-ip / sh-ip), so the skills are complementary and mutually reinforcing without a justified developmental dependency. relatesTo is symmetric with null direction and retains canonical endpoint order. judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade 2 (rank 2) WRITING > Handwriting, so direction must follow Term order within the grade. The second SFI is Grade 2 Term 1 ('Forms 26 lower and upper case letters correctly: directionality, formation and spacing within lines'); the first SFI is Grade 2 Term 2 ('Aligns writing properly on 17 mm ruled lines'), confirmed by identity_scope_values term=term 1 and term=term 2 and by the distinct Term ancestors (cc9e8c34 TERM 1, f5c1edcd TERM 2). This is substantive extension rather than generic repetition: Term 1 establishes correct letter formation, directionality and spacing within lines, and Term 2 applies that control to placing/aligning whole pieces of writing on narrower 17 mm ruled lines (the Term 2 row context refers to copying and writing longer and more varied pieces neatly). Proficiency in accurate letter formation and spacing within lines supports success in aligning writing on ruled lines, so buildsTowards runs from the Term 1 skill (second) to the Term 2 skill (first); the reverse (later Term to earlier Term within one Grade) is not permitted. Both endpoints have truncated source evidence (24 omitted items each) and upstream merge/audit context on endpoints and ancestors, so the judgment rests on the bounded excerpts supplied.
